transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-05-07 16:00 UTC | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Lena Park, Omar Singh (Redwood); Judy Alvarez, Mark Chen, Priya Rao (ACME ML)

Summary: Weekly POC check-in focused on cost/unit economics, tokens per second per dollar, caching savings observed in last run, and tuning batching tradeoffs. Action items and next steps agreed at end.

[00:00:05] Lena Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll do the usual 30ish minute sync plus time for questions, um, primarily cost and perf today.
[00:00:15] Judy Alvarez: Yep thanks, and real quick we had a small incident this morning with the test harness timing out, but it's resolved, should not affect the numbers we pulled yesterday.
[00:00:28] Mark Chen: thanks, yeah we restarted the runner.
[00:00:32] Omar Singh: OK cool, so I sent the updated spreadsheet earlier — it's the tokens per second per dollar view. Quick recap: last week we saw about 450 tokens/sec on the hosted endpoint at default batching, unit cost around $0.0028 per 1k tokens after discounts, so tokens/sec per dollar was roughly 160k tokens per dollar-hour equivalent — rough numbers, I can walk through the sheet.
[00:01:05] Priya Rao: can you repeat that slowly? tokens per dollar, I want to understand how that maps to our cost model.
[00:01:12] Omar Singh: sure — so imagine you pay $1, you get X tokens processed per second on average over an hour — it's a way to normalize throughput to spend. For our numbers: 450 tokens/sec when batching was at default and no KV prefix cache; cost math gives about 160k tokens per dollar.
[00:01:35] Judy Alvarez: those defaults were with request-level batching of 8, right?
[00:01:40] Omar Singh: correct, batch size target 8, max latency SLO of 200ms.
[00:01:44] Lena Park: important to note those were mixed-length prompts, some long conversations so real-worldish.
[00:01:50] Mark Chen: what did enabling KV caching do to that number? we tried a short run last night.
[00:01:55] Omar Singh: good question — enabling prefix/KV cache for the hot paths bumped tokens/sec to about 700 tokens/sec and effectively increased tokens per dollar to ~250k. So roughly a 55% improvement in throughput for that workload slice. But caveat, your hit rate matters — that run had about a 65% cache hit for prefixes.
[00:02:20] Priya Rao: 65% hit — our real traffic might be lower because we have many unique user prompts. Is there a cardinality threshold where caching becomes ineffective?
[00:02:29] Omar Singh: yes, if hit rate drops below ~25-30% you start seeing diminishing returns vs the overhead of managing cache. But even low hit rates can reduce latency for repeated system prompts or shared prefixes.
[00:02:41] Judy Alvarez: we need to quantify cost of cache storage vs savings; is that captured?
[00:02:46] Omar Singh: in the spreadsheet there's a line for cache storage cost (per GB-month) and estimated cache population churn. For this POC we approximated storage at $0.08/GB-month, negligible compared to per-token inference, but we also modeled cache miss penalties in latency.
[00:03:01] Mark Chen: and batching tradeoffs — if we increase batch target to 16, what happens?
[00:03:06] Omar Singh: moving to target batch 16 increased tokens/sec to ~1100 in the hosted runs, so that helps tokens per dollar a lot, but median latency climbed from ~120ms to ~220ms and 95th pct from ~340ms to ~520ms — so it trades latency for cost efficiency.
[00:03:26] Priya Rao: our SLOs are 200ms median and 500ms p95. 95th at 520ms is worrying.
[00:03:33] Lena Park: yeah that's right, so we recommended a mixed strategy: route high-priority traffic to lower-batch paths and bulk/async traffic to high-batch paths — Redwood's smart routing can do that.
[00:03:44] Judy Alvarez: how complex is that to implement in our stack? we don't want to add heavy routing logic.
[00:03:49] Omar Singh: Redwood can do it via route policies — you tag requests with priority and set batch profiles per route. Minimal changes to app code: a header or flag. We can help set defaults.
[00:03:59] Mark Chen: Any perf delta between hosted vs dedicated for batch efficiency?
[00:04:05] Omar Singh: dedicated tends to be more consistent. For the same batch settings, dedicated GPUs gave us ~10-20% better tokens/sec due to higher sustained throughput and less noisy neighbors, and p95 latencies were steadier. But dedicated has fixed cost — you need to justify via sustained volume.
[00:04:21] Priya Rao: from a procurement perspective we need to know break-even utilization. Did the sheet show that?
[00:04:26] Omar Singh: yes, break-even was around 60% sustained utilization of reserved capacity for your projected traffic over 3 months. I can highlight that cell.
[00:04:34] Judy Alvarez: are quantization/4-bit models in play here? we saw a model variant with int8 quant that looked cheaper but maybe lower quality.
[00:04:42] Omar Singh: we included a quantized variant in the model catalog rows — quantized gave ~2x tokens/sec for same cost but you may see slight regressions on long-context coherence; we recommend spot-check evals on your prompt set.
[00:04:56] Lena Park: also, there's a hybrid option — use quantized for stateless stuff like embeddings or short replies, and full-precision for core dialog.
[00:05:04] Mark Chen: ok that helps. On caching: what about eviction churn? our users' phrases change daily.
[00:05:10] Omar Singh: eviction policy matters — TTL-based or LRU, and we saw in your logs a median prefix reuse window of ~12 hours, which is reasonable. If your prefix churn is daily, caching still helps for repeated system prompts and a subset of users.
[00:05:23] Judy Alvarez: are the cache metrics exposed in the console? we need hit rate, population size, evictions, miss latency.
[00:05:29] Lena Park: yes console has per-route cache metrics and tracing hooks; we can drop a dashboard link.
[00:05:34] Priya Rao: about the tokens/sec per dollar metric — is that normalized for peak vs sustained? we pay for bursts differently.
[00:05:41] Omar Singh: the sheet has two columns: sustained-hour equivalent and burst scenario. Burst costs are higher because you pay higher on-demand capacity; tokens/sec per $ in bursts was ~30% worse in our sample.
[00:05:51] Mark Chen: can Redwood autoscale quicker to avoid burst surcharge? we saw slow scale-up on another vendor.
[00:05:58] Omar Singh: Redwood supports fast warm pools and predictive scaling based on traffic patterns; dedicated reserved pools can also have burst capacity options. We can demo a warm-pool config in the next session.
[00:06:08] Judy Alvarez: any security notes for dedicated? we'll need KMS and audit logs.
[00:06:12] Lena Park: Private and Dedicated both support KMS/HSM, audit logs, SSO and RBAC — we included relevant SOC2 info in the security pack we shared.
[00:06:20] Priya Rao: good.
[00:06:22] [00:06:22] -- quick audio glitch, speaker overlap --
[00:06:28] Omar Singh: sample recommend tuning for your next run — three configs: conservative (batch 8, kv cache off), balanced (batch 8, kv cache on), aggressive (batch 16, kv cache on + quantized model). The sheet has cost and latency estimates for each.
[00:06:44] Judy Alvarez: can you put the config as exact flags we can paste into our test harness?
[00:06:49] Omar Singh: yes — I'll include JSON snippets and a runnable perf script in the follow-up.
[00:06:55] Mark Chen: we want to test the balanced config end-to-end with our real traffic for 1 hour and share logs.
[00:07:01] Priya Rao: agreed. Also can you add a column in the sheet with 95th pct latency per config? that's critical.
[00:07:07] Omar Singh: will do.
[00:07:10] Lena Park: quick question from me — any blockers on the ACME side to run the balanced config this week?
[00:07:15] Judy Alvarez: just time to schedule the run, but otherwise no infra blockers.
[00:07:19] Mark Chen: I'll provision the runner and forward logs to Omar.
[00:07:23] Priya Rao: timeline — we'd like to decide on Dedicated vs Hosted by end of month, so these runs are high priority.
[00:07:30] Lena Park: understood — we'll prioritize the benchmark and the cost spreadsheet so you can do break-even analysis.
[00:07:35] [00:07:35] --- mid-call summary by Lena ---
[00:07:40] Lena Park: recap so far: KV cache materially increases tokens/sec if hit rate >~40%; batching increases tokens/sec and reduces $/token but hurts p95; Dedicated improves consistency and throughput at fixed cost; break-even around 60% utilization. Action items assigned.
[00:08:00] Priya Rao: sounds right. Any surprises from last week's run we should highlight?
[00:08:05] Omar Singh: one surprise: during the 3am test we saw a small tail event tied to a particular long prompt that caused KV misses and a spike in latency. We added a guardrail to route very long contexts to a separate pathway.
[00:08:20] Judy Alvarez: that was our system prompt concatenation issue — we'll fix how we stitch history.
[00:08:25] Mark Chen: ok we'll patch that.
[00:08:28] [00:08:28] -- 1 minute of background talking while sharing spreadsheet --
[00:09:40] Omar Singh: moving into Qs: Priya, you had asked about dedicated pricing options for seasonal peaks?
[00:09:46] Priya Rao: yes — if we go dedicated, can we have burst credits or a hybrid plan so we don't pay double during peak?
[00:09:53] Omar Singh: we offer burst capacity add-ons and also a hybrid routing policy: baseline on dedicated, overflow to hosted during peaks. Pricing for overflow is pay-as-you-go, but the blended effective $/token can still be lower than pure on-demand if reserved utilization is high.
[00:10:08] Judy Alvarez: on observability — can we get token-level cost broken down by route and model in the console?
[00:10:14] Lena Park: yes, per-route cost breakdown and token-level cost visualization exist; we can grant access to a demo org.
[00:10:20] Mark Chen: one last technical: does increasing batch size risk OOMs on GPU for large sequence lengths?
[00:10:26] Omar Singh: it can — batch * seq_len * model_size is the driver. We have dynamic batching and memory-aware scheduling; for very long contexts we cap batch size and prefer asynchronous paths. We'll include settings to avoid OOMs.
[00:10:40] Priya Rao: great.
[00:10:43] [00:10:43] --- final recap and next steps ---
[00:10:45] Lena Park: recap actions: Omar will run and share perf script and configs, Lena will send updated spreadsheet (tokens/sec/$ with sustained and burst columns), Judy/Mark will run the balanced config for 1 hour and share logs. We'll schedule a deep benchmark session next week to compare dedicated vs hosted with the same traffic.
[00:11:05] Judy Alvarez: thanks, we'll aim to run asap and share by Friday.
[00:11:09] Mark Chen: I'll set up the runner and forward access.
[00:11:12] Priya Rao: thanks everyone.
[00:11:15] Lena Park: thanks, we'll follow up with the artifacts — Lena ends call.

Notes: Transcript includes occasional transcription artifacts and overlap. Relevant shared artifacts: link: /redwood/poc/acme-ml/cost-breakdown-20250507.xlsx (referenced), link: /redwood/poc/acme-ml/perf-configs/balanced.json (referenced).

End of transcript.
